queries.query: the Cherokee picture of the world as a body of land afloat on the ocean, hung from the stone sky by ropes at its four corners, doomed to go under when they wear out
queries.note: 'Great island floating in a sea of water', 'suspended at each of the four cardinal points by a cord', 'sky vault' paraphrased into ropes, corners, stone sky.

queries.query: the sons of Kana'ti trail their father into the mountains and find where he keeps all the deer shut away under a great stone
queries.note: Origin of game; 'turn over a large stone that appeared to be carelessly leaned against another', 'lets one out and kills it' paraphrased; 'Kana'ti' kept as the hunter's name.

queries.query: seven men carry a box to the ghost country in the west to bring back the spirit of the Sun's daughter, warned never to lift the lid before reaching home
queries.note: The Daughter of the Sun; 'Tsusgina'i', 'the Darkening land', 'strike her with the rods' paraphrased; the Sun's daughter kept as the tale's title figure.

queries.query: the captured Shawano wizard buys his life by killing the great horned serpent Uktena, striking its one vulnerable spot and carrying off the blazing crystal from its head
queries.note: Agan-unitsi's search; 'arrow through its heart, which was under the seventh spot', 'blazing star set in the forehead', 'Ulunsuti' paraphrased; 'Uktena' kept.

queries.query: why do stories tell of people rising into the sky to become a cluster of stars
queries.note: The seven boys who danced up into the sky as the Pleiades; star-cluster origin tales are pan-traditional. No target — graded post-hoc.

queries.query: how can a river be revered as a living being that speaks to and purifies people
queries.note: The Long Man river god whose voice is the cataract; sacred rivers are answered by many traditions. No target — graded post-hoc.
